transfers.source_mechanism: adaptive network formation through exploratory probes and reinforcement of efficient pathways
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: distributed adaptive network optimization through local exploration and reinforcement of efficient traffic flow patterns
transfers.required_translation: replace protoplasm with traffic signal controllers, replace nutrients with vehicle flow, replace exploratory probes with signal timing experiments, replace network connections with communication between adjacent intersections
transfers.expected_effect: traffic signal network that adapts to real-time conditions by reinforcing timing patterns that improve flow and retracting patterns that cause congestion
boundary_conditions: limited communication between adjacent intersections only
local measurements only (vehicle count and queue length)
transfers.testable_prediction: after implementing the adaptive system, the average intersection delay during unexpected incidents will decrease by at least 20% compared to the current system within the first 15 minutes of an incident, without requiring central re-optimization
